RagShortTexts: Situated across critical crossroads, Armenia maintained fortified border networks anchored against rivers, mountain passes, and dense forests.
Under intense pressure from migrating populations and rival expansion, the borders faced acute strain from regional upheavals.
Frontier governors exercised broad emergency prerogatives, maintaining patrol outposts and garrison bastions to shield agrarian heartlands.

Variants.Content: The territorial perimeter of Armenia spanned treacherous terrain encompassing river crossings, mountain defiles, and primeval woodlands. Shielding the arterial supply corridors leading toward Vagharshapat & Artashat, the regime garrisoned fortified outposts and watchtowers tasked with round-the-clock reconnaissance. In 374 AD, strategic volatility reached a fever pitch, aggravated by border clashes and cross-frontier raiding. Provincial commanders operated under persistent resource deficits, forced to contain covert banditry while preparing against full-scale royal invasions, knowing that any fatal rupture along the forward limes would unleash catastrophic devastation upon undefended inland communities.

A watchman on the high pass lights a torch at dusk and waits for the answering flame from the next ridge. Patrols descend into the gorges to check for hidden bands of raiders, and the garrison doctor asks each returning man whether his wounds came from arrows or from the cold. The fort's gate stays chained until the signal tower confirms that the road is clear.

The marzban's courier arrived with news that Persian troop movements have been seen along the western passes, and our frontier forts remain short of grain. Quietly propose to the Iberian and Albanian lords an exchange of hostages for a mutual defense of the mountain roads. Keep the terms out of the royal chancery until the envoys confirm that the other side will honor the arrangement.
